look_here_first: Look for a sprawling or twining vine with thickened storage roots and highly variable heart-shaped to deeply lobed leaves. Flowers, when present, are pale pink to lavender morning-glory funnels with a darker throat.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Current Kew POWO treats Ipomoea batatas as native from Mexico south through tropical Central America to northern South America, and introduced in Texas.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Cultivated, escaped, or naturalized Texas occurrences do not count as native target-zone evidence.

best_field_traits: leaves highly variable: cordate, triangular, hastate, or palmately lobed
pale pink to lavender funnel-shaped flowers when present
frequent cultivated or escaped garden/agricultural plant
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with I. cordatotriloba, sweet potato is usually more robust and associated with cultivation, often with conspicuous storage roots and more variable, sometimes deeply lobed foliage. Do not treat escaped plants as Texas-native.

comparisons.key_distinctions: I. cordatotriloba is a native tievine without cultivated sweet-potato storage roots and typically has shorter, broader sepals with ciliate margins. I. hederacea has longer, narrower sepals and annual morning-glory habit.
